hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected.

hazards.name: High-speed multi-lane roadway
hazards.description: The wide roadway with multiple through lanes and minimal friction encourages high vehicle speeds directly adjacent to residential housing.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tanker truck on the right side of the road creates a significant blind spot for both drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Curb Cut Width
hazards.description: The parking lot entrance creates a massive, undefined conflict zone where vehicles can cross the pedestrian path at any point along the block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center background, where the parking lot meets the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Unprotected Roadway
hazards.description: The multi-lane road lacks any pedestrian refuge or marked crossings, requiring a long, unprotected crossing distance.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground spanning the width of the road.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no buffer zone, planting strip, or parked cars to protect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Degraded roadway surface
hazards.description: A large, uneven pavement patch in the roadway could affect vehicle handling or create a trip hazard if pedestrians cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway in the immediate foreground.

hazards.name: Pavement Cracking
hazards.description: Visible cracks in the roadway surface near the intersection could affect vehicle handling or create minor trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No visible pedestrian signals to manage right-of-way at this wide crossing.

hazards.name: Frequent Curb Cuts
hazards.description: Multiple vehicle access points across the sidewalk on the left side increase the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes with minimal traffic calming encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential context.

hazards.name: Multi-lane Threat
hazards.description: Pedestrians must monitor four or more lanes of traffic, where vehicles in one lane may obscure pedestrians from drivers in adjacent lanes.

hazards.name: Wide Travel Lanes
hazards.description: The generous width of the roadway and lack of vertical traffic calming elements may encourage high vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a large expanse of asphalt, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Slip lane
hazards.description: The right-turn slip lane allows vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning, creating a conflict point with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image where the road diverges

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can hide pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the far curb where cars are parked near the crossing area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to provide a safe waiting area and reduce the unprotected crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a marked mid-block crossing with continental markings and pedestrian warning signage.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reconfigure the roadway to reduce the number of through lanes, slowing traffic and shortening crossing distances.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the crosswalk to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the gas station driveway to slow turning vehicles and minimize the conflict zone.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair cracked concrete slabs and clear debris from the vacant lot to ensure a smooth, level walking surface.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and personal security after dark.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings with high-visibility paint and signage to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while also helping to calm traffic speeds.

interventions.title: Streetscape Improvements
interventions.description: Planting street trees or installing a furniture zone would create a physical buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Paint center lines and parking lane markings to organize traffic flow and visually narrow the street to encourage slower speeds.

interventions.title: Slip-Resistant Grate Covers
interventions.description: Apply high-friction coatings or replace existing grates with ADA-compliant, slip-resistant versions to improve pedestrian stability.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical barrier and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture and planting zone with street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet and Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the number or width of travel lanes to slow vehicle speeds and provide space for a pedestrian buffer or bike lanes.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation
interventions.description: Narrow and define the parking lot access points to reduce the width of the vehicle-pedestrian conflict zone.

interventions.title: Curb-side Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a vegetated buffer or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians using the walkway at night.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or curb extensions to slow vehicle speeds on this residential block.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signals to clearly indicate when it is safe to cross and how much time remains.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a raised median refuge island to break up the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Install raised islands in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Slip Lane Redesign
interventions.description: Tighten the turn radius or convert the slip lane into a standard right turn to slow vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to naturally slow vehicle speeds and reclaim space for pedestrian infrastructure.
